title: Stitchboard: Rapid run index (personal compact tracker)
content:
Purpose: handheld running index for quick comparison of tiny experiments. Keep it short, prioritize runs I can reproduce in <1 hour.

Columns: RUN_ID | DATE | MODEL | QUANT | BATCH | PREFIX_CACHE | TOKENS/REQ | AVG_MS | P95_MS | P99_MS | COST/1kTOK | NOTES | VERDICT

001 | 2025-11-12 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 1 | off | 64 | 42 | 78 | 120 | $0.85 | baseline single-shot, no cache | ok
002 | 2025-11-12 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 4 | off | 256 | 110 | 190 | 310 | $0.60 | batching helps throughput but p99 large variance | marginal-for-prod
003 | 2025-11-13 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 4 | on | 256 | 48 | 92 | 130 | $0.20 | prefix cache reduced p99 significantly (warm paths) | recommended-explore
004 | 2025-11-13 | llama-2-13b | q4_0 | 1 | off | 64 | 85 | 160 | 280 | $1.70 | single-shot, heavier model; noticeable tail | expensive
005 | 2025-11-14 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 8 | on | 512 | 80 | 140 | 220 | $0.18 | big batch = better unit cost, p99 still ok with cache | good-candidate
006 | 2025-11-15 | meta-llama-7b | q3_km | 4 | on | 256 | 62 | 120 | 190 | $0.12 | q3 quantization drops latency slightly, quality spot-check needed | needs-eval
007 | 2025-11-16 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 4 | on | 1024 | 95 | 210 | 380 | $0.11 | long context inflated p99; KV cache warms but memory thrash? | investigate-kv-eviction
008 | 2025-11-18 | meta-llama-7b | q4_0 | 2 | on | 128 | 36 | 68 | 115 | $0.32 | sweet spot for latency-sensitive small prompts | keep

Quick notes / heuristics observed:
- Prefix cache on => p99 often drops ~50-70% for re-requested prefixes; huge win for chat-like flows.
- Small batch (1-2) best for latency-first; batch 4+ only if user-level concurrency is expected.
- q3_km looks promising for unit cost but need prompt-quality spot checks on MMLU subset.
- Long contexts (>=1024 tokens) blow up p99 unless cache gets >90% hit rate.

Repro steps (one-liner):
- checkout branch: feature/kv-cache-tuning; docker run local-infer:latest; script run_quick.sh --model meta-llama-7b --quant q4_0 --batch 4 --cache on --seed 42 --iters 120

ToDo / short backlog:
- [ ] Run q3_km full sweep vs q4_0 on our 100-prompt eval set (quality + CTR). JIRA-ML-842 (assigned Maya).
- [x] Add cost/1k calculation column (done 2025-11-12).
- [ ] Add automatic p99 alert example to Redwood Console dashboard (small spike example).
- [ ] Try structured warmup (priming first 50 reqs with synthetic traffic) to measure steady-state p99.

Open questions / friction points:
- Why did run 007 show high p99 despite cache on? hypothesis: cache eviction due to oversized KV row for 1024 context + GPU memory fragmentation. Need trace.
- How to standardize COST/1kTOK across quant modes (some backends bill based on compute-time not tokens) — normalization step defined?

Scratch math (approx):
- cost_per_1k = (avg_ms_per_token * $/ms_gpu + model_mem_surcharge) * 1000 -> placeholder; I use measured cost from infra billing for small runs then backfill formula.

Quick links I referred to during runs:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache/pull/112
- Eval set (gdrive): https://drive.google.com/open?id=evals/mini-100
- Trace ticket: JIRA-OPS-1192

Immediate next experiment (next week):
- Sweep: batch in {1,2,4}, cache {on,off}, quant {q4_0,q3_km}, context {128,512} — aim: find three operating points: latency-first, cost-first, balanced. Keep each cell 3 runs, seed variance.

Personal notes-to-self (informal):
- If p99 variance > 2x between runs, capture full perf traces and restart runtime between configs.
- Keep this file terse; move cleaned results to /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/bench-results when stable.

End of stitchboard entry.
